Context: The following section focuses on human blood types.
Content: Human blood types are categorized based on the `text(ABO)` blood group system. In this system, an individual has `text(one)` of `text(four)` different blood types: `text(A)`, `text(B)`, `text(AB)`, or `text(O)`. These `text(four)` blood types result from interactions of the alleles `bbtext(A)`, `bbtext(B)`, and `bbtext(O)`.

The `bbtext(A)`, `bbtext(B)`, and `bbtext(O)` alleles code for various forms of an enzyme involved in the production of molecules called antigens. Antigens are found on the surface of red blood cells. The table shows how the `text(three)` alleles interact.

A person who needs a blood transfusion must receive a compatible blood type. If the person receives an incompatible blood type, their immune system will react to the antigens in the blood by producing proteins called antibodies. The antibodies will attack the antigens, causing the blood to clump in the person’s blood vessels. To prevent such complications, blood-type compatibility is always tested before a blood transfusion.
